Job Description
The Future Talent Program features internships that last 10-12 weeks and will include one or more projects. These opportunities in our Research Division can provide you with great development and a chance to see if we are the right company for your long-term goals.
Our Pharmaceutical Analysis & Digital Technology (PADT) and Large Molecule Analytical (LMA) departments in Rahway, NJ, West Point, PA, Boston, MA, and South San Francisco, CA are seeking summer interns who will work collaboratively in a team environment at our state-of-the-art laboratories to develop novel analytical methodologies that impact drug substance and drug product development. Day-to-day research for the intern will focus on solving key challenges in product and process characterization.
The summer interns will be exposed to:
Core instrumentation critical for modern analysis of small molecules, biologics, and/or vaccines, for manufacturing process characterization, and for determination of drug substance and/or drug product chemical, physical, and biological attributes.
Fundamentals of analytical, physical, and biological chemistry method development necessary to solve problems as a member of an integrated team in support of the small and large molecule pipeline at our company.
The PADT and LMA departments will expose the intern to various expert groups in the areas of screening and high-throughput analysis, molecular and physical materials characterization, structural elucidation including high end mass spectrometry and NMR techniques, separation-based techniques, assays for interrogating critical attributes of drug products, immunoassays, cell-based assays, labeled-compound analyses, trace metals analyses, and advanced statistical and data analytics/ machine learning processes, further broadening their experience. 
The interns in PADT and LMA will also participate in departmental and project team meetings to provide a broad perspective on the drug development process in the pharmaceutical industry. The interns will be responsible for accurate electronic notebook recording of experimental details and for analysis and interpretation of data that may be used for internal or external scientific publications which may follow from the internship. Interns will have the opportunity to gain further knowledge and skill sets via refinement of laboratory skills, introduction to new analytical techniques, exposure to current challenges in analytical research, and perspective on the practical aspects of drug development. In addition, the intern will have an opportunity to present their research results in both oral and written formats.
We are seeking intern candidates at all academic levels (undergraduate and graduate) with strong academic performance, communication skills, teamwork, and the ability to work in a multi- functional environment.
Locations: Rahway, NJ; West Point, PA; Boston, MA; South San Francisco, CA
This is a full-time summer internship position.
Education Requirements:
Candidates must be a currently enrolled student pursuing a Bachelor's, Master’s, or PhD degree in Chemistry, Biology (e.g. Cell Biology, Virology), Biochemistry, Chemical/Biological Engineering, Materials Science, Pharmaceutical Science, or a related discipline.
Required Experience and Skills:
Candidates must be available to work full-time for 10-12 consecutive weeks beginning in May or June of 2027.
Candidates must have completed at least (2) years of study toward a bachelor's degree by June 2027.
Preferred Experience and Skills:
Candidates should have significant interest in analytical sciences for small molecules, vaccines, and/or biologics.
Candidates should have basic laboratory skills and research experience, such as: lab notebook recording, use of analytical instrumentation, analysis and interpretation of data, and safe lab practices.
Candidates should have a GPA of 3.0 or higher.

Our company is on a quest for cures and is committed to being the world’s premier, most research-intensive biopharmaceutical company. Today, we’re doubling down on this goal. Our Research & Development Division is a true scientific research facility of tomorrow and will take our company’s leading discovery capabilities and world-class small molecule, vaccines, and biologics R&D expertise to create breakthrough science that radically changes the way we approach serious diseases.
Our Research & Development Division's Biologics Process Research and Development (BPR&D) department is seeking summer interns who will work collaboratively in a team environment at our state-of-the-art laboratories to develop novel bioprocess technologies and solve key challenges in biopharmaceutical process development and manufacturing. BPR&D is responsible for developing manufacturing processes and associated technologies for our company's biologics pipeline. BPR&D includes three main technical functional areas/groups: Process Cell Sciences (PCS) which also interfaces with our company’s discovery teams, Biologics’ Process Development (BPD) which includes both upstream and downstream bioprocessing, and US-based Manufacturing Operations (USMO). This job posting covers opportunities for interns in all the above three functional areas.
The summer interns will be exposed to:
Fundamentals of bioprocessing, which are necessary to solve problems as a member of an integrated team in support of the large molecule pipeline at our company.
Expert groups in the areas of cell line development and engineering, upstream and downstream process development, high throughput screening, media development, -omics, and continuous bioprocessing
State-of-the-art bioprocessing approaches, automation and engineering technologies, equipment, and facilities used for manufacturing modern biopharmaceuticals.
The interns in BPR&D will also participate in departmental and project team meetings to provide a broad perspective on the drug development process in the pharmaceutical industry. The interns will be responsible for accurate electronic notebook recording of experimental details and for analysis and interpretation of data that may be used for internal or external scientific publications which may follow from the internship. Interns will have the opportunity to gain further knowledge, and skillsets via refinement of laboratory skills, introduction to new experimental techniques, exposure to current challenges in bioprocess research, and perspectives on the practical aspects of drug development. In addition, the intern student will have an opportunity to present their research results in both oral and written formats.
This is a full-time internship position wherein we are seeking intern candidates at all levels with strong academic performance, communication skills, teamwork, and the ability to work in a multi-functional and fast-paced environment.
Locations: Rahway, NJ; Boston, MA; South San Francisco, CA
Education:
Required: Candidates must be a currently enrolled student pursuing a Bachelor's, Master’s, or PhD degree in Chemistry, Biology (e.g. Cell Biology, Virology), Biochemistry, Engineering (Chemical, Mechanical, Electrical), Materials Science, Pharmaceutical Science or a related discipline.
Required Experience and Skills:
Candidates must be available to work full-time for 10-12 consecutive weeks beginning in May or June of 2027
Candidates must have completed at least 2 years of study toward a Bachelor’s degree by June 2027
Preferred Experience and Skills:
Candidates should have significant interest in biopharmaceuticals or facilities/maintenance.
Candidates should have basic laboratory skills (lab notebook recording, use of instrumentation, analysis and interpretation of data, and safe lab practices), research experience, along with a problem-solving attitude.
For USMO - Candidates should have familiarity with engineering tools such as computer-aided design (CAD) software, Distributed Control Systems (DCS)/ Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC), data historians and piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs)

The Logistics Analyst Summer Intern will support the Logistics Center of Excellence team in advancing global transportation and warehousing strategies through data analysis, procurement event support, scenario modeling, and continuous improvement. This role is designed for a highly analytical, curious, and collaborative student who is interested in supply chain, logistics, procurement, and digital transformation.
The intern will work with regional logistics, field, supply chain, procurement, operations, and finance stakeholders to help improve cost visibility, strengthen sourcing outcomes, quantify value creation, and identify opportunities to optimize end-to-end material flows.
Key Responsibilities
RFP Development and Facilitation
Support the development and facilitation of transportation and warehousing RFPs across global regions.
Assist regional teams in validating inputs to and outputs from procurement events, including lane data, volume assumptions, service requirements, rate structures, and award recommendations.
Manage data and requirements templates that ensure alignment across regional stakeholders, procurement teams, logistics leaders, and operating teams.
Pressure test and verify procurement event results to confirm accuracy, completeness, and alignment with business requirements.
Develop tools and reporting approaches to quantify value after implementation, including cost savings, service impacts, and compliance to awarded strategies.
Impact Analysis and Scenario Development
Support regional teams in quantifying the impact of off-cycle changes across all modes of transportation and warehousing.
Analyze cost, service, capacity, supplier, and operational impacts associated with changes to logistics networks, carrier selections, warehousing models, or transportation requirements.
Develop alternative scenarios to minimize unfavorable impacts while maintaining business continuity and service expectations.
Document required process, supplier, stakeholder, or system changes needed to implement alternative scenarios effectively.
AI Tools, Reporting, and Carrier Optimization
Create AI-enabled tools and reports that leverage available data across regions to assess opportunities to optimize carrier selection across transportation modes.
Compile, cleanse, and analyze data from regional logistics, procurement, payables, finance, and operations sources to identify trends, gaps, and improvement opportunities.
Build dashboards, templates, or analytical models that improve visibility to logistics spend, carrier performance, implementation progress, and value capture.
Continuous Improvement Opportunity Identification
Leverage site visits across regions to understand logistics process flows, stakeholder pain points, and opportunities to reduce cost or improve service.
Collaborate with field, supply chain, operations, procurement, finance, and logistics stakeholders to identify opportunities that add value across end-to-end material flows.
Support the development and implementation of programs to track the value of procurement savings and productivity initiatives across regions.
Use available payables data to connect initiative value to measurable P&L impact.
Prepare concise summaries, recommendations, and progress updates for leadership reviews and regional working sessions.
Education
Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in supply chain management, logistics, operations, business analytics, industrial engineering, data analytics, finance, or a related field.
Must be actively pursuing a degree and remain enrolled in an accredited degree program following the internship start date in Summer 2027.
Qualifications
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work with large data sets and draw actionable conclusions.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint; experience with Power BI, Power Query, Python, SQL, or other analytics tools is preferred.
Interest in artificial intelligence, automation, digital tools, and their application to supply chain and logistics decision-making.
Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional and regional stakeholders.
Comfort working in a fast-paced, matrixed environment with multiple priorities and evolving business needs.
Demonstrated curiosity, ownership, attention to detail, and willingness to learn from both data and direct site engagement.
Internship Learning Outcomes
Hands-on exposure to global logistics strategy, transportation sourcing, warehousing operations, and supplier management.
Practical experience supporting RFP events, procurement analytics, value tracking, and logistics impact assessments.
Experience using data and emerging AI tools to solve real business problems and improve decision-making.
Opportunities to collaborate across regions and functions while building executive-ready communication and presentation skills.
Understanding of how logistics savings and productivity initiatives connect to operational performance and P&L impact.
Ideal Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate is data-driven, resourceful, and comfortable moving between analysis, stakeholder engagement, and practical implementation. This individual should be eager to learn how logistics decisions are made across regions and motivated to create tools, insights, and processes that improve cost, service, visibility, and value capture.
The hourly range for this role is $20/hr to $23/hr. We may pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may change in the future. Pay within the salary range will be based on factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

“Stand Out. For Good”. At Altar’d State, those four words are more than just our motto, they are why we exist. Supply Chain Internship
Our Supply Chain team plays a critical role in supporting our stores, e-commerce business, and continued growth. We are seeking a motivated and curious Supply Chain Intern who is eager to gain hands-on experience within a fast-paced retail distribution environment.
The Supply Chain Internship is based on-site at our Distribution Center in Maryville, Tennessee. This program is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of how products move through our supply chain—from receipt at the Distribution Center through delivery to our stores and e-commerce guests.
During the first two weeks of the internship, Supply Chain Interns will actively perform key Distribution Center processes alongside our associates and operational leaders. This hands-on experience will include:
Picking e-commerce orders

Learning Distribution Center safety, quality, productivity, and inventory-control standards

Vendor Compliance: Understand vendor requirements, inbound product quality, labeling, packaging, and compliance processes.
Transportation: Gain exposure to inbound and outbound transportation, carrier management, delivery performance, and freight costs.
Data Analytics: Use operational data to identify trends, evaluate performance, and support continuous-improvement opportunities.

Develop an end-to-end understanding of retail supply chain and Distribution Center operations.
Work alongside Distribution Center associates and leaders.
Participate in cross-functional Supply Chain rotations and team meetings.

Prepare and present observations, findings, and recommendations at the conclusion of the internship.
Follow all Distribution Center safety policies and operating procedures.

Self-motivated, adaptable, and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.

This internship is an on-site position based at the Distribution Center in Maryville, Tennessee.

Business Leadership Program Internship Overview:
Synchrony’s Business Leadership Program Summer Internship is a 10-week paid assignment in one of our 10 Tracks. During the summer, each BLP Intern is provided with project work that is important to our business, and we’ll look to you to challenge us and contribute to driving innovation for our future. Beyond the assignment, BLPs gain the full Synchrony Experience with an immersive orientation during Week 1, the Intern Summer Series to meet and network with leaders around the business, and ongoing support from a team and mentors who are invested in your success.
Analytics & Strategy In Credit BLP Internship Experience: What You’ll Accomplish
This internship is for students who are looking to get a critical jump start on a career in Analytics & Strategy In Credit, working side by side with our experts in the function to gain valuable hands-on experience. We perform the mission-critical work of deciding who is accepted for loans, how much credit we should extend to them and for how long. An Analytics & Strategy In Credit BLP will gain insight into the strategy, operations and growth of our business, as well as the broader industry.
In the Analytics & Strategy In Credit BLP Internship, you will:
Learn the process of fairly and responsibly extending credit–including underwriting and managing loan portfolios, and mitigating fraud
Help clients achieve the right balance of growth and loss mitigation
Use advanced analytics techniques to develop and implement strategies that drive business decisions
Understand the entire account credit lifecycle and the impact of credit performance on the Profit & Loss Statement
Have the opportunity to work close to our Client partners as part of our Client teams
Work with sophisticated probabilistic models and maintain relationships with Credit Bureaus and scoring vendors
What do we look for in all potential BLP Interns?
Ability to effectively work independently and within collaborative teams
Proven leadership both inside and beyond the classroom
Strong project management and communication skills
Demonstrated flexibility, adaptability, and passion for learning
Passion for excellence with high integrity and a commitment to quality
Relevant experience or demonstrated interest in area of work
Desired Characteristics for the Analytics & Strategy In Credit Track
Academic excellence with financial, quantitative and analytical competency
Analytical skills, ability to synthesize complex information, process-oriented
Critical reasoning, problem-solving ability, creative thinking, and intellectual curiosity
Prioritization and time management skills
Strong work ethic, passion for excellence with high integrity, and commitment to quality
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Software: SAS, Python, Machine Learning
Modeling skills plus experience with financial statements P&L statements (cash flow a plus)

Pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Mathematics, Finance, Economics or relevant major
Excellent academic record – Minimum overall 3.0 GPA

Make IT Personal at TD SYNNEX through our Early Careers Summer Internship Program. This 10-week Commercial, High Growth Track is an experience designed for business students who are ready to sharpen their commercial and customer-facing skills, explore go-to-market career pathways, and contribute to meaningful work across a global IT distributor.
This application is for students interested in Sales, Marketing, Vendor Management, Business Development, Product Management, and Data Analytics. Applicants will be asked to indicate their preferred area of interest when applying.
The program runs 10 weeks, full time, beginning May 17, 2027, with internships hosted in Greenville, SC and Clearwater, FL.
Each internship is aligned to a department and business function, giving students the opportunity to apply classroom learning to real commercial projects in partner engagement, marketing, and revenue growth. Interns will build professional networks through senior leader speaker sessions, peer engagement events, job shadowing, and exposure to the business operations behind a global IT distribution company.
Applications for the 2027 Summer Internship Cohort will close at 11:59 PM on Sunday, January 3rd. Students are encouraged to submit their materials early to ensure full consideration.
What We Are Looking For
Pursuing a business-related major, including Marketing, Sales or Professional Selling, Business Administration and Management, Supply Chain Management, International Business, Communications, Economics, or a related field
Current undergraduate student with junior standing or above by summer 2027, including May 2027 graduates
Authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship
Available to work full time, 40 hours per week, for the full 10-week program
Able to work from one of the listed locations on a hybrid schedule of three plus days per week in office
Proficient in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook, with comfort building presentations and customer-ready materials
Preferred: familiarity with AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot, and an interest in using technology to strengthen outreach, content, and business outcomes
Strong written and verbal communication skills and comfort working with partners and internal stakeholders
Interest in contributing to a values-driven culture guided by Together, We Own It; We Dare to Go; We Grow and Win; and We Do the Right Thing
Example Duties and Projects
Sales Intern
Support the Sales team with contracts, procurement processes, and compliance documentation
Generate quotes, track orders, and provide sales support for federal and public sector clients
Act as a liaison between vendors, clients, and internal teams to keep communication timely and fulfillment accurate
Join client meetings and work with account managers to align solutions with customer needs
Example project: support a federal sales workflow from quote preparation and vendor coordination through fulfillment tracking, then present recommendations that improve client satisfaction and efficiency
Marketing Intern
Partner with marketing and services teams to create promotional content for key business units
Design and publish internal newsletters that build awareness and adoption of our services
Develop one-pagers, LinkedIn content, and presentation materials that support messaging and outreach
Maintain content submission forms and refresh case studies so they stay accurate and relevant
Example project: support a service-focused marketing campaign from content creation and layout design through scheduling and handoff, then present recommendations to improve future messaging and engagement
Vendor Management Intern
Help maintain vendor records, update contact information, and keep data accurate across internal systems
Partner with vendors and internal teams to resolve invoice discrepancies, shipment issues, and payment variances
Support account reconciliation by validating invoices, reviewing aged receivables, and monitoring vendor account health
Work with cross-functional teams, including Product Management, Procurement, and Warehouse Operations, to resolve issues on time
Example project: complete a vendor account reconciliation, research invoice discrepancies with internal teams, and present recommendations that streamline vendor communication and reduce aged balances
Business Development Intern
Support the Public Sector Business Development team by identifying vendor and reseller partners with limited alignment to federal, state, local, education, and healthcare markets
Conduct data sourcing and gap analysis across partners to uncover engagement opportunities and guide targeted enablement
Help organize strategic events that promote vendor solutions and encourage collaboration
Work with internal stakeholders and external partners to support pipeline growth, contract awareness, and market expansion
Example project: support a partner engagement initiative by mapping public sector contacts, identifying gaps, coordinating outreach, and presenting recommendations that improve alignment and drive growth
Product Management Intern
Support product lifecycle management by assisting with vendor onboarding, quote creation, and special pricing requests
Partner with vendors and internal teams to streamline communication, improve efficiency, and support sales enablement
Build and maintain reseller pursuit lists and vertical alignment strategies that strengthen vendor relationships and support quarterly business reviews
Manage quote extensions, license renewals, and add-on requests that help retain and grow vendor partnerships
Example project: support a vendor growth initiative by building targeted reseller lists, coordinating with vendors, and presenting outcomes and strategies for future engagement
Data Analytics Intern
Work within a finance team to clean, flag, and extract data, ensuring quality before it reaches reporting and analysis
Build machine learning forecasting models to predict account balances and anticipate trends, transactions, and cash flow changes
Analyze reports, semantic models, and workspace usage to improve how the business uses its data
Work with tools including Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, PySpark, and scikit-learn, with support toward earning a Microsoft certification
Present findings to business partners, translating analysis into recommendations they can act on
Example project: build a forecasting model end to end from data cleaning and model selection through validation, then present results and planning implications to the team
Selected interns will complete a background check before the program begins.
Housing may be available in Greenville, SC, for eligible students.
Participation in TD SYNNEX early careers programs, including the internship program does not guarantee an offer of, or placement into, a permanent position with TD SYNNEX. At the conclusion of the program—or at any point during the program—participants may be released from the role based on performance outcomes, business needs, or failure to meet TD SYNNEX policies or procedures."
Actual annual compensation offered will be based on several variables including geographic location, work experience, education and skills/ achievements, and will be mutually agreed upon at the time of offer. The Discovery Representative Program average starting rate is approximately $22.00 per hour.

What’s In It For You?
Elective Benefits: Our programs are tailored to your country to best accommodate your lifestyle.
Grow Your Career: Accelerate your path to success (and keep up with the future) with formal programs on leadership and professional development, and many more on-demand courses.
Elevate Your Personal Well-Being: Boost your financial, physical, and mental well-being through seminars, events, and our global Life Empowerment Assistance Program.
Diversity, Equity & Inclusion: It’s not just a phrase to us; valuing every voice is how we succeed. Join us in celebrating our global diversity through inclusive education, meaningful peer-to-peer conversations, and equitable growth and development opportunities.
Make the Most of our Global Organization: Network with other new co-workers within your first 30 days through our onboarding program.
Connect with Your Community: Participate in internal, peer-led inclusive communities and activities, including business resource groups, local volunteering events, and more environmental and social initiatives.
Don’t meet every single requirement? Apply anyway.
At TD SYNNEX, we’re proud to be recognized as a great place to work and a leader in the promotion and practice of diversity, equity and inclusion. If you’re excited about working for our company and believe you’re a good fit for this role, we encourage you to apply. You may be exactly the person we’re looking for!
We are an equal opportunity employer and committed to building a team that represents and empowers a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, genetics, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Other benefits for eligible team members include 401(k), employee discount, short term disability, long term disability, paid sick leave, paid national holidays, and paid vacation.
ALL ABOUT TARGET
Working at Target means helping all families discover the joy of everyday life. We bring that vision to life through our values and culture. Learn more about Target here.
ALL ABOUT THE STORES EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP
Experience firsthand what it’s like to lead a retail team within a Target store. This internship is a paid 40 hr/week, hands-on training program to develop and prepare you for store leadership. As a Stores Executive Intern, you will get a valuable realistic preview of the Executive Team Leader role (Assistant Store Manager) over a defined period of time. Within this store management internship, you will work closely with other managers and team members to develop an understanding of how Target’s retail business works and what it takes to excel in a management role. You will be introduced to multiple areas of the store’s business, but the majority of your time will be spent leading amongst the team, identifying and working towards store priorities, and delivering great guest service.
This program is designed to teach individuals how to lead within a retail store and you will:
Learn how to drive guest experience and impact your store’s financial, team, and operational performance.
Work alongside a mentor and learn how they effectively lead their department within the store.
Have the opportunity to step into leading your mentor’s departments- of course, we will be there to guide you and help you learn along the way!
Spend your days learning to lead and motivate a team, drive sales results, merchandise products, and provide an exceptional experience for our guests.
Have ongoing development conversations, as your development will be a top priority of ours.
Lead and support the execution of daily operations by working with your team members to build culture and guide your team to grow and achieve goals.
Learn more from past Interns, Mentors, and Managers here.
At Target, we believe in our leaders having meaningful experiences that help them build and develop skills for a career. The goal of the Stores Executive internship is to provide a realistic job preview of an ETL role. The role of a Stores Executive Intern can provide you with the skills and experience of:
Guest service fundamentals and experience building and managing a guest-first team culture across the store
Guest engagement; problem-solving and resolution
Retail business fundamentals
Setting and planning department(s) monthly/quarterly workload to support business priorities and managing a team to deliver service and sales goals
Managing a team of hourly team members and team leaders while creating business strategies and goals
Recruiting, selecting and talent management of hourly team members and leaders
As a Stores Executive Intern, no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will most likely include the following responsibilities:
Spending time on the store salesfloor and backroom leading team members and aligning the team on daily business priorities
Working alongside your Executive Team Lead (ETL) mentor and other leaders in the building to gain an understanding of their roles
Leading through daily priorities (stocking shelves, ensuring a safe and welcoming environment that’s inviting to guests, helping build displays within the store, etc.)
Partnering with leaders regarding team member performance by teaching, coaching, training, and delivering timely performance feedback
Addressing team member concerns and removing hurdles to ensure smooth operations and goal attainment
Leading/presenting at daily huddles with peer/leadership team
Planning daily goals and organizing plans within the building
Providing summary of results and priorities with peer/leadership team
Working with store leaders each day to set goals and expectations
Reviewing business reporting and guest insights to understand, troubleshoot and follow up on opportunity areas.
Delivering an exceptional guest experience by ensuring team members are knowledgeable and empowered to make it right for guests
Providing new ideas and recommend solutions to business or team opportunities
Taking the initiative to learn how to be a Target leader by seeking out opportunities for growth and development; continuously learning throughout the internship experience
Commit to learning Target’s expectations of leaders and use them to personally develop by asking questions and seeking feedback
Actively participate in internship program training activities, developmental opportunities and events
Demonstrate a willingness to take strategic risks and take on new assignments
Demonstrate a culture of ethical conduct, safety, and compliance; lead the team to work in the same way and hold others accountable to this commitment
Work in a safe manner at all times to benefit yourself and others; identify and correct hazards; comply with all safety policies and best practices
Foster an inclusive, equitable, safe, and secure culture
Carry out principal duties and responsibilities by the department
Gain an understanding of all business areas to develop business acumen
Create a welcoming experience by greeting guests as you are completing your daily tasks.
When guests need assistance, engage with guests in a welcoming way, to help solve their specific needs
Thank guests and let them know we’re happy they chose to shop at Target
All other duties based on business needs
ALL ABOUT YOU
This may be the right job for you if:
You enjoy interacting and helping others - including guests that shop our store and fellow team members you work with.
You thrive in a fast-moving, highly active and physically demanding role, where teamwork, flexibility, and creative problem solving are key to success.
You are open to working a flexible work schedule with varying hours, days or shifts (including nights, weekends, holidays and other peak shopping times).
The good news is that we have some amazing training that will help teach you how to be an effective leader within our stores. But there are a few things you need from the get-go:
Previous retail experience preferred, but not required
Strong interest in working in retail, specifically within our stores in management
Leadership skills and team-oriented thinking
Learn and adapt to current technology needs
Work independently and as part of a team
Manage workload and prioritize tasks independently
Welcoming and helpful attitude
Effective communication skills
We are an awesome place to work and care about our teams, so we want to make sure we are clear on a few more basics that we expect:
Access all areas of the building to respond to guest or team member issues
Interpret instructions, reports, and information
Accurately handle cash register operations as needed
Climb up and down ladders as needed
Scan, handle and move merchandise efficiently and safely, including frequently lifting or moving merchandise up to 44 pounds
Ability to communicate on multiple frequency devices and operate handheld scanners, and other technology equipment as directed
Flexible work schedule (e.g., nights, weekends and holidays) and reliable and prompt attendance necessary

Learn how to drive guest experience and impact your store’s financial, team, and operational performance.
Work alongside a mentor and learn how they effectively lead their department within the store.

Spend your days learning to lead and motivate a team, drive sales results, merchandise products, and provide an exceptional experience for our guests.
Have ongoing development conversations, as your development will be a top priority of ours.
Lead and support the execution of daily operations by working with your team members to build culture and guide your team to grow and achieve goals.
Learn more from past Interns, Mentors, and Managers here.

Guest service fundamentals and experience building and managing a guest-first team culture across the store
Guest engagement; problem-solving and resolution
Retail business fundamentals
Setting and planning department(s) monthly/quarterly workload to support business priorities and managing a team to deliver service and sales goals
Managing a team of hourly team members and team leaders while creating business strategies and goals
Recruiting, selecting and talent management of hourly team members and leaders

Spending time on the store salesfloor and backroom leading team members and aligning the team on daily business priorities
Working alongside your Executive Team Lead (ETL) mentor and other leaders in the building to gain an understanding of their roles
Leading through daily priorities (stocking shelves, ensuring a safe and welcoming environment that’s inviting to guests, helping build displays within the store, etc.)
Partnering with leaders regarding team member performance by teaching, coaching, training, and delivering timely performance feedback
Addressing team member concerns and removing hurdles to ensure smooth operations and goal attainment
Leading/presenting at daily huddles with peer/leadership team
Planning daily goals and organizing plans within the building
Providing summary of results and priorities with peer/leadership team
Working with store leaders each day to set goals and expectations
Reviewing business reporting and guest insights to understand, troubleshoot and follow up on opportunity areas.
Delivering an exceptional guest experience by ensuring team members are knowledgeable and empowered to make it right for guests
Providing new ideas and recommend solutions to business or team opportunities
Taking the initiative to learn how to be a Target leader by seeking out opportunities for growth and development; continuously learning throughout the internship experience

Actively participate in internship program training activities, developmental opportunities and events

Carry out principal duties and responsibilities by the department
Gain an understanding of all business areas to develop business acumen

When guests need assistance, engage with guests in a welcoming way, to help solve their specific needs
Thank guests and let them know we’re happy they chose to shop at Target
All other duties based on business needs

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.
BACKGROUND: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. At work in over 40 countries and 28 U.S. cities to restore safety, dignity and hope, the IRC leads the way from harm to home. The IRC in Atlanta office was established in 1979 and has resettled over 30,000 refugees from 67 countries into the Greater Atlanta area. As the largest refugee resettlement agency in Georgia, the IRC in Atlanta resettles an average of 1,000 refugees into Georgia annually and provides additional services and assistance to another 2,500 refugees and asylees.
SCOPE OF ADULT EDUCATION INTERN WORK: The IRC’s Adult Education Intern assists refugee and immigrant adults in ESL classes to develop the language skills critical for success. The classes aim to build vocabulary and communication skills, convey skills necessary for the American workforce, and impart information about integral life skills and systems so that clients can be successful and productive members of their communities, that they can be civically engaged, and so that they can pursue career pathways of their choice. Please note that all internship positions are unpaid.
These classes meet regularly three days per week, Tuesday through Thursday, for 3-hour class sessions, with both in-person and online class options, and offer instruction to adult students at varying levels of English proficiencies, from Basic to Advanced. Year-round classes operate with rolling enrollment and new students are oriented and placed into classes and levels weekly. Classes are multi-level meaning multiple levels will be represented within a single class and interns and other class assistants allow for multiple breakout groups to separate students by their proficiency level. Instruction is focused on developing literacy, comprehension, and confidence to apply towards real world situations including dealing with housing issues, shopping, the K-12 public school system, public transportation, employment, healthcare, and other daily life skills.
Adult Education interns work under class lead instructors and other IRC Adult Education staff to effectively engage with prospective and current immigrant and refugee clients. This can include a variety of ongoing activities such as:
Recruitment and Outreach: providing information about programming, schedule, and expectations around education services.
Intake and Orientation: working with clients individually to complete enrollment documents, to discuss goals, and schedule a formal proficiency level assessment
Classroom Support: assisting lead instructors with classroom management activities, following developed curriculum and leading instruction with groups of English language learners.
Classroom Support is expected to be a primary activity for nearly all Adult Education interns.
Retention and Follow-up: conferencing with, surveying, and connecting with current and former participants, assessing goals and identifying appropriate referrals
Adult Education interns in Summer 2026 will work with both virtual classes and with in-person classes, working with students joining classes through online platforms and with students attending at the IRC in Atlanta’s main office.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Teaching groups of students in multi-level classes following curriculum developed by lead instructor.
Assist instructor in developing and implementing multi-level comprehension and literacy activities.
Supporting outside-of-class functions of the Adult Education program in recruitment and outreach, intake and orientation, classroom support, and retention and follow-up activities.
Support program activities by researching new curriculum content and preparing educational materials as requested by instructor.
Submit intern hours on volunteer dashboard.
Other duties as assigned.
QUALIFICATIONS:
Interns must have
Strong communication skills: communication between instructors and fellow class assistants before, during, and after classes, and communication with adult Education language learners during classes.
Availability for at least 9 hours of class time per week.
An interest in or experience with teaching in generally and teaching ESL specifically.
An interest in working closely with a diverse population of adults.
Comfortability in working in a cross-cultural environment, in-person, online, and over the phone, with adult learners, sometimes with little or no English proficiency.
Comfortability in working with a variable number of students (individually and in groups).
Ability to work in a collaborative environment and in co-teaching.
Comfortability in adapting learning activities with limited notice.
Fluent in spoken and written English. Bi-lingual abilities are not necessary but can be a plus.
REQUIREMENTS:
Must submit intern hours on volunteer portal.
Must pass a background check.
Commitment of 9 hours per week for a minimum of 3 consecutive months.
Must be at least 18 years old.
Must be authorized to work in the United States. Please note that we are unable to provide sponsorship for a US work authorization.
This is a hybrid role. This role reports to the Adult Education Instructional Supervisor.
The internship will be filled on a rolling basis. We will continue to accept applications until August 14th, 2026, or until the position is filled, whichever occurs first. Internship will begin the week of September 8th, 2026.
PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS
All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.
Cookies: https://careers.rescue.org/us/en/cookiesettings
US Benefits: We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.
Equal Opportunity Employer: IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Are you ready to make a real impact? At Vertex, our mission is to tackle serious diseases and to change lives, for the better, for the future. Your Impact
The Vertex Process Development Co-Op is a 6-month experiential training program for students currently working towards an advanced degree in Biological Sciences, Chemical Sciences, or other related fields. If you are passionate, collaborative, and growth-minded, a co-op at Vertex will help you gain meaningful experience in our Drug Product Development functional areas and serve as a launchpad for your career.
The application deadline for this co-op is November 15th.  What you will be doing: 
The Drug Product Development team within Process Development is responsible for developing scalable, high-quality drug product processes to advance Vertex’s Cell and Gene Therapy programs from early development through manufacturing readiness.
This Co-op position offers the opportunity to contribute to a high-impact cryopreservation process development project for Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) drug product. The role will focus on establishing a cryo-microscopy workflow to evaluate cryoprotective agent (CPA) diffusion into islets and characterize islet responses across different cryoprotective formulations and cryopreservation conditions. By integrating experimental imaging data with computational modeling, the Co-op will characterize CPA diffusion kinetics, inform formulation development, and identify opportunities to optimize key cryopreservation parameters. This experience offers hands-on exposure to cell therapy drug product development and collaboration with cross-functional teams advancing innovative therapies for people living with T1D.
Key Responsibilities:
Over the course of this 6-month Co-op, the individual will contribute to the following project deliverables:
Establish a standardized cryo-microscopy workflow for real-time imaging of stem cell-derived islets during CPA loading, unloading, and controlled freeze/thaw cycles, including sample preparation, staining, imaging, and data-capture procedures.
Design and execute cryopreservation studies using selected CPA formulations and loading/unloading strategies, generating cryo-microscopy datasets to characterize islet morphology and response across conditions.
Develop an initial computational modeling framework that complements experimental cryo-microscopy data. Model the correlation between CPA diffusion kinetics, islet size and morphology, and cryopreservation process parameters.
Integrate experimental and computational results to characterize CPA diffusion kinetics and islet response across formulations and process conditions. Use findings to identify promising CPA formulations and loading/unloading strategies and guide next steps for screening and cryopreservation process optimization.
Maintain detailed, accurate records of experimental activities, methods, data, analyses, and conclusions in electronic laboratory notebooks (ELNs). Author study reports, technical summaries, and standardized protocols for the established cryo-microscopy and computational modeling workflows.
Qualifications:
Currently pursuing a graduate degree (PhD and master’s are preferred); or undergraduate degree in Cell Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Biomedical Engineering, Bioengineering, Chemical or Biochemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Computational Biology, or a related scientific discipline.
Experience with mammalian cell culture, including aseptic technique, routine cell culture handling, media preparation, and sample preparation; experience with stem cells or stem cell-derived products is preferred.
Foundational knowledge of cell cryopreservation and hands-on experience with cell freezing and thawing; experience with cell aggregates, spheroids, organoids, or other three-dimensional cell systems is a plus.
Experience with cell microscopy, including sample preparation, cell staining, image acquisition, and image-based evaluation; experience with cryo-microscopy is a plus.
Knowledge of and/or experience with computational modeling approaches relevant to molecular dynamics, diffusion kinetics, or cryopreservation processes.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with the ability to independently troubleshoot experimental challenges, manage priorities, and maintain accurate documentation and attention to detail in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
Highly motivated and collaborative team player with strong communication skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to learn new techniques while contributing to complex, high-impact process development work.
